newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hopes for deal with Japan on port row.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hopes for deal with Japan on port row.

text.p: A U.S.-Japan agreement in a dispute over access to Japanese ports is still uncertain as a deadline for imposing U.S. sanctions looms, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Friday.
But a senior official, speaking on condition of anonymity, was more upbeat. "The talks are going okay. We hope for an agreement" this weekend, the official said.
Burns, at a news briefing, said both sides "obviously want an agreement (but) it's hard to predict where we're going to come out today."
Officials said privately that the Washington talks would probably continue over the weekend as the U.S. side, at least, was keen to conclude them before Monday, the deadline for sanctions.

From that day, the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission has said it will impose penalties of $100,000 per visit on Japanese carriers calling at American ports if Tokyo does not move quickly to open access to Japanese ports.

The United States contends its shipping firms are treated unfairly by Tokyo, which maintains tight controls on the licensing of stevedores and port operations in Japan. U.S. firms want to be able to hire their own stevedores and set up their own operations, claiming they could save money and improve productivity.
